---
title: "Software"
---

I write open-source software for genomics in C, C++, R, Rust and Python, tested
with continuous integration and released through five registries (Bioconductor,
CRAN, Bioconda, PyPI and crates.io). The tools are built for genome-scale data, and
I keep maintaining what I release: universalmotif has been in continuous development since 2018 and has been
downloaded more than 150,000 times.

## universalmotif

An R package for importing, exporting, converting, scanning and comparing biological
sequence motifs, with its performance-critical code written in C++. I have written
and maintained it since 2018, and it has been downloaded more than 150,000 times
across Bioconductor and Bioconda.

[Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/universalmotif) ·
[GitHub](https://github.com/bjmt/universalmotif) ·
[Paper (JOSS, 2024)](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07012)

The package also has Rust and Python versions. The Rust crate covers most of what
the R package does, is checked against it, and is the multithreaded engine behind
the Python package, which returns numpy arrays and polars DataFrames.

- Python: [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/universalmotif/) ·
  [Documentation](https://bjmt.github.io/universalmotif-py/) ·
  [GitHub](https://github.com/bjmt/universalmotif-py)
- Rust: [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/universalmotif) ·
  [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/universalmotif) ·
  [GitHub](https://github.com/bjmt/universalmotif-rs)

## quaqc

Quality control and filtering for ATAC-seq data from any genome, written in C on top
of htslib and built for large multi-sample studies: in the documented example it
processes around 80 million *Arabidopsis* ATAC-seq reads in about a minute. It also
works for other unspliced sequencing data such as ChIP-seq. A companion R package,
quaqcr, wraps quaqc and adds tools for analysing and plotting its results.

[Bioconda](https://bioconda.github.io/recipes/quaqc/README.html) ·
[GitHub](https://github.com/bjmt/quaqc) ·
[Paper (Bioinformatics, 2024)](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btae649)\
quaqcr: [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=quaqcr) ·
[GitHub](https://github.com/bjmt/quaqcr)

## Machine learning on regulatory sequence

I train deep sequence-to-function models of chromatin accessibility, ChromBPNet in
TensorFlow and seq2PRINT in PyTorch, on single-cell ATAC-seq data from about 30,000
*Arabidopsis* cells. The work covers training from scratch and fine-tuning,
evaluating accuracy and biases, and interpreting predictions with attribution and
feature ablation (more on the [Research](research.qmd#models-of-regulatory-sequence)
page). universalmotif draws the contribution-weight motifs that these models
produce.

## Other tools

- [bwtk](https://github.com/bjmt/bwtk): conversion, merging, subsetting and
  transformation of bigWig and bedGraph files (C).
  [Bioconda](https://bioconda.github.io/recipes/bwtk/README.html)
- [yamtk](https://github.com/bjmt/yamtk): genome-scale scanning and enrichment of
  transcription factor binding sites (C).
- [bam2td](https://github.com/noborilab/bam2td): builds HOMER tag directories
  directly from SAM, BAM or CRAM files, handling CIGAR operations that HOMER's own
  parser gets wrong (C).
- [msaviz](https://github.com/bjmt/msaviz): visualisation of multiple sequence
  alignments as ggplot2 heatmaps or lollipop charts, fast even for alignments with
  millions of residues (R).

## Data resources

- [TAIR12 blacklist](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20084760): regions of the TAIR12
  *Arabidopsis* assembly with anomalous signal in sequencing experiments, to filter
  out of ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq analyses. Generated with the ENCODE Blacklist pipeline
  to match the TAIR10 blacklist of Klasfeld et al. (2022), with Tatsuya Nobori.
  [GitHub](https://github.com/noborilab/TAIR12_blacklist)

## Pipelines

For the Nobori group I built
[csRNAseq_pipeline](https://github.com/noborilab/csRNAseq_pipeline), a tested and
containerised Snakemake workflow for csRNA-seq, together with
[bfqutils](https://github.com/noborilab/bfqutils) (FASTQ trimming, merging and
analysis in C) and [tssUtils](https://github.com/noborilab/tssUtils) (transcription
start site analysis in R).

## Earlier projects

- [PhyloCorrelate](https://phylocorrelate.uwaterloo.ca): a database and R package for
  inferring bacterial gene functional associations from phylogenetic profiles.
  [GitHub](https://github.com/bjmt/phylocorrpkg)
- [DiffBase](https://diffbase.uwaterloo.ca): a classification of *C. difficile*
  toxin subtypes. [GitHub](https://github.com/doxeylab/diffBase)
- [PathFams](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-021-07982-8): statistical detection of
  pathogen-associated protein domains.
- [mirlyn](https://github.com/escamero/mirlyn): diversity analysis of amplicon
  sequencing data with repeated rarefying, to account for the uncertainty that
  rarefying introduces (R).
  [Paper (Scientific Reports, 2021)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-01636-1)
